newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-FERGUSON REAPS BENEFITS OF EXTENDED TRIP TO GERMANY.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-FERGUSON REAPS BENEFITS OF EXTENDED TRIP TO GERMANY.

text.p: Manchester United manager Alex Ferguson seems to have found the answer to his side's end-of-season fatigue -- an extended trip to Germany.

The English champions stayed on an extra day after their 1-0 defeat by Borussia Dortmund in the European Cup on Wednesday instead of flying home in the middle of the night to prepare for their tricky weekend fixture at Blackburn.

The decision appeared to have reaped benefits on Saturday when an authoritative and relaxed United beat their Lancashire rivals 3-2 to retain a three-point lead in the race for the premier league title.
"We decided to stay on in Germany a little bit longer rather than facing a long trip back at two o'clock in the morning," Ferguson said.
"Instead we had an extra day there which I think did us good, especially as the facilities in Germany were excellent.
"I think it was the right thing to do on this occasion."
"I thought that was a very, very good performance by us today, especially at this stage of the season. The players looked good and they really had the bit between their teeth."
United won the match at Ewood Park despite a penalty miss from Eric Cantona mid-way through the first half.

They took the lead through Andy Cole, went 2-1 up thanks to a Paul Scholes' goal after Billy McKinlay had equalised for Blackburn, and then sealed a vital victory with a strike from Cantona nine minutes from time.

Blackburn, a shadow of the side that pipped United to the league title in 1995, pulled a goal back in the closing minutes through Paul Warhurst, but seldom looked capable of upsetting Ferguson's side.

United now face a hectic run-in to the season, with five league matches and a second leg tie against Dortmund to squeeze in before the premier league deadline of May 11. In nine days between May 3 and May 11, they are scheduled to play four times.

United have requested an extension to the season to allow them to play Newcastle after the deadline, but Liverpool and second-placed Arsenal have both complained that would give the champions an unfair advantage.
On Friday the Premier League rejected United's request. United responded by vowing to appeal against the decision through the Football Association (F.A.).
Ferguson, who recently launched a stinging attack on Arsenal manager Arsene Wenger for opposing United's stance, remained tight-lipped about the simmering dispute on Saturday.
When asked if he felt his outburst against Wenger had made United more unpopular in the country at large, he simply smiled and asked: "How unpopular can we get?"
"We're just hoping, touch wood, that by the time we get to the last week of the season we don't have any injuries," he said.
But Blackburn caretaker manager Tony Parkes said United should not be allowed to play their final match of the season after all their rivals had finished their campaigns.
"We can't have an extention to the season, although I can see United's point and they do appear to be being punished for their success," he said.
"But you can't have odd teams playing after the end of the season. If there is to be an extention is has to be for everyone."
He said he saw no evidence United were tiring as a result of their heavy schedule.
"We just accept that they're going to be a totally committed United at three o'clock on a Saturday afternoon, and they didn't disappoint us in that respect."
United's legal experts are reportedly preparing a letter to send to the F.A. complaining of the fixture congestion, but it will be some time before a solution is reached.
In the meantime, Ferguson could do worse than take his battle-weary players on another relaxing trip to Germany.
